You have learned to cast spells. The rules on spellcasting are in the Player's Handbook; below is how you use them as a Warrior of the Mystic Arts.

Cantrips. You know two Sorcerer cantrips of your choice; @UUID[Compendium.compendium-owidyn.spells.Item.52K6rs5zHagiRUsB]{Blade Ward} and @UUID[Compendium.compendium-owidyn.spells.Item.klxpZKnseduoTKqh]{Thunderclap} are recommended. Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one of them with another Sorcerer cantrip. At Monk level 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice.

Spell Slots. The Warrior of the Mystic Arts Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells you can cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Sorcerer spells; @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplJump000000]{Jump}, @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplMagicMissi]{Magic Missile}, and @UUID[Compendium.dnd5e.spells24.Item.phbsplShield0000]{Shield} are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the table; the chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Monk level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.

Multiclassing. If you multiclass and have the Spellcasting feature from more than one class, add one third of your Monk levels (round down) to determine your spell slots.
